: The page buttons and row count below a table made with `opt_interactive()`, in place of a
  **GTI table**'s **control bar**. Its style is set with `opt_interactive(pagination_type=...)`.

Panel
: In a **GTI table**, a box opened from a button in the **control bar**: the Columns panel (to
  hide and move columns), the grouping panel (to group the rows by a column), the export panel
  (from `~~GTI.i_export()`), and the info panel, which says how the table is sorted and can go
  back to the view it was first shown with.

Pinned columns
: In a wide **GTI table** that scrolls sideways, columns that stay in view, on the left (after the
  **stub**, which always stays) or on the right. Set with `~~GTI.i_cols_pin()`.

Preheader
: Optional content rendered above the table element itself (before the **header**). Set via
  `tab_header(preheader=...)`. Accepts raw HTML strings and is useful for adding
  non-tabular content like badges or links that sit outside the table's visual boundaries.

Preset
: The settings a **GTI table** starts with, chosen with `GTI(preset=...)`: `"report"` (the
  default), for a table to be read, or `"explorer"`, for looking through data, with every column
  filtered, profiled, hideable and movable, compact monospaced rows, CSV export, and the
  **row numbers** and **status line** of `~~GTI.i_inspect()`. The `i_` methods change a preset
  as they would any table.

Query
: A **GTI table**'s **filters** written as text, such as `mfr in ("Ferrari") and hp >= 600`. The
  `{ }` button in the **control bar** opens the query for readers to edit, and
  `~~GTI.i_view(filter=...)` takes one to set the filters the table starts with.

Responsive layout
: How a **GTI table** fits a container narrower than itself, set with `~~GTI.i_responsive()`:
  `"scroll"` (the table scrolls sideways), `"stack"` (each row becomes a card, below
  `stack_below=` pixels), or `"collapse"` (columns are dropped by their priority from
  `~~GTI.i_cols_priority()`, and each row gets a button showing what was dropped). The default,
  `"auto"`, picks one from the table's columns.

Row details
: In a **GTI table**, more content for each row, shown under it when the reader clicks the arrow
  by the row (or uses Expand all in the info **panel**). Made from each row's values by a
  function given to `~~GTI.i_row_details()`, or taken from a column.

Row group
: A categorical label that divides the **body** into logical sections of rows. Row groups
  appear as spanning labels across the full width of the table. Created by passing
  `groupname_col=` to `GT()` and ordered with `row_group_order()`. Targetable with
  `loc.row_groups()`.

Row numbers
: In a **GTI table** with `~~GTI.i_inspect()`, the number at the start of each row giving its
  place in the data, which stays with the row as the table is sorted and filtered. A DataFrame's
  rows are numbered from 0 and a database's from 1, unless `row_start=` says otherwise.

Row selector
: An expression passed to a `rows=` parameter to identify which rows an operation should act
  on. Accepts an integer index, a list of indices, a list of row names (when a **stub** is
  present), a Polars expression, or a callable. Row selectors are used in methods like
  `~~GT.fmt_number()`, `tab_style()`, `cols_merge()`, and others.

Search
: In an **interactive table**, a field that keeps the rows with what's typed in any searchable
  column's cells, as the table shows them, ignoring case and accents. In a **GTI table** it's in
  the **control bar** (with `~~GTI.i_search()`, on by default) and is opened with `/`.

Selection
: The rows a reader has selected in a **GTI table** with `~~GTI.i_selection()`, by clicking the
  rows or their checkboxes (one row with `"single"`, any number with `"multiple"`). The selection
  links **linked tables**, can be exported, and can be read from Python.

Source note
: Citation or attribution text displayed in the **footer**, below any **footnotes**. Added
  with `tab_source_note()` and supports `md()` and `html()` formatting. Multiple source notes
  can be added and appear in the order they were defined. Targetable with `loc.source_notes()`.

Spanner label
: A label in the **column header** that spans across multiple contiguous **column labels**,
  providing a higher-level grouping. Created with `tab_spanner()` or automatically with
  `tab_spanner_delim()` (which splits column names at a delimiter character), and relabeled with
  `tab_spanner_label_with()`. Spanners can be nested to any depth. Targetable with
  `loc.spanner_labels()`.

Status line
: In a **GTI table** with `~~GTI.i_inspect()`, the line just above the table saying what the data
  is and how much of it is shown (e.g., "Polars DataFrame · 12 of 47 rows × 4 columns").

Stub
: A reserved leftmost column of the table that holds row labels, visually set apart from the
  **body** by a vertical dividing line. Created by passing `rowname_col=` to `GT()`. The stub
  provides a way to name rows and is required for row-based selection by name. Targetable with
  `loc.stub()`. The `stub` sentinel object (importable from `great_tables`) can be used in
  `cols_width()` to set the stub column's width.

Stubhead
: The cell at the top-left corner of the table, at the intersection of the **stub** and the
  **column header**. It exists only when a **stub** is present and can be labeled with
  `tab_stubhead()`. Targetable with `loc.stubhead()`.

Style
: A visual property applied to table elements via `tab_style()`. Styles are defined using
  objects from the `style` module: `style.text()` for text properties (color, font, size,
  weight, alignment), `style.fill()` for background color, `style.borders()` for cell borders,
  and `style.css()` for arbitrary CSS. Styles are paired with **location selectors** to target
  specific parts of the table.

Subtitle
: Secondary descriptive text displayed below the **title** in the **header**. Set via
  `tab_header(subtitle=...)`. Supports `md()` and `html()` formatting. Targetable with
  `loc.subtitle()`.

Summary rows
: Aggregation rows placed within each **row group** that summarize that group's data. Created
  with `summary_rows()`, which accepts aggregation functions (Polars expressions or callables)
  and an optional formatter. Can be placed at the top or bottom of each group with the
  `side=` parameter. Targetable with `loc.summary()`.

Table theme
: A coordinated set of visual options that control the overall appearance of the table.
  **Great Tables** provides 36 premade themes via `opt_stylize()`, combining 6 visual styles with 6
  color palettes. Fine-grained control over every aspect of the table's appearance is available
  through `tab_options()`.

Title
: The main heading text displayed at the top of the **header**. Set via
  `tab_header(title=...)`. Supports `md()` and `html()` formatting. Targetable with
  `loc.title()`.

View
: How a reader has a **GTI table** set up: its **filters**, sort, **search**, page, page size,
  hidden columns, the column its rows are grouped by, and the height of a body that scrolls. The
  view the table starts with is set with `~~GTI.i_view()`. See also **view state**.

View state
: A **GTI table**'s **view** as it's kept with `~~GTI.i_view_state()`: in the page's URL, so a
  reloaded or shared page opens the table as it was, and optionally in the browser's storage
  (`storage=True`). It also gives the **control bar** undo and redo buttons. Keeping the view in
  the URL needs a table ID.


### The Zen of Great Tables

Python has a well-known easter egg: `import this` prints *The Zen of Python*
([PEP 20](https://peps.python.org/pep-0020/)). **Great Tables** took inspiration from *this* and
wrote its own Zen. And since it's a Zen about tables, importing it in a notebook shows a great table:

```{python}
import great_tables.this
```

At the console, the import prints the aphorisms as plain text instead, just like `import this`
does. To see the table from there, open it in your browser:

```python
from great_tables.this import table

table().show()
```

```{=html}
<script src="../assets/tabblen.js" defer></script>
<div style="margin-top: 2rem; text-align: center">
  <gt-tabblen mood="zen" arms="open" bubble="top" cell-trick="zen" intro='[["wait", 800], ["say", "Simple is better than complex.", 3500]]'></gt-tabblen>
</div>
```
